subject: Renewal: NovaCare uplift accelerator, co-term & license-swap options
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lawrence <emma.lawrence@novacare.com>, Hector Ramos <hector.ramos@novacare.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: NovaCare uplift accelerator, co-term & license-swap options

Hi Emma / Hector —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Per our conversation, I pulled together three pathways that match the usage patterns you shared and the timelines procurement mentioned. Attached is a brief usage snapshot (Usage_Snapshot_Q1_2027.xlsx) to ground the numbers.

High-level options (short: cost delta, commit impact, legal effort):

1) Accelerator top-up (fastest, lowest legal overhead)
   - One-time uplift to reserved capacity for Q3–Q4 (pro-rata billing for remainder of year)
   - 8–12% discount on per-token rate depending on committed units
   - No contract end-date change (stays annual)

2) Annualize + co-term (preferred for predictability)
   - Move to 12-month committed reserved pool, co-term with your existing contract end date (Nov 2027)
   - 12–18% blended discount based on tiered commits + onboarding credit
   - Requires a short amendment (we can e-sign)

3) License-swap to reserved units (highest upside, moderate legal)
   - Swap seat/license budget into a reserved capacity commitment (blended pricing)
   - Up to 22% effective discount vs current pay-as-you-go when combined with 12-month commit
   - Best if you expect sustained usage growth and want predictable unit economics

Quick asks from our side so we can put formal numbers together:
- Target co-term preference: keep Nov 2027 or push to Dec 2027?
- Procurement timing (PO deadline) and required paperwork (procurement_form.pdf)?
- Any constraints on on-prem/VPC usage or data residency we should account for?

If you want, Kimberly and I can run a modeled quote for each option with your Q1–Q2 run-rate and share example invoices. Happy to jump on a 30-min call this week to walk through trade-offs.

Next steps suggestion: choose 1 preferred path, we send a draft amendment + cost table, you share procurement timeline and any legal must-haves.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: Usage_Snapshot_Q1_2027.xlsx

From: Emma Lawrence <emma.lawrence@novacare.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: NovaCare uplift accelerator, co-term & license-swap options

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear options. A few clarifying items from procurement and engineering before we pick a path:

- Procurement target: we need a PO in place by 2027-05-10 to include in our May financials.
- Our preferred co-term would be Nov 2027 if possible (aligns with other vendors).
- Can you show a 12-month cost run-rate for both Accelerator top-up and the License-swap (example: current avg monthly spend = $137k; projected month 6 = $190k)?
- Procurement asked if we can get a modest onboarding / ramp credit if we sign before 2027-05-03 — helps cover initial training/ingestion costs.

Technical/legal Qs (cc'ing Hector, procurement):
- Any SLA change if we move to reserved? Need 99.95% or equivalent for our production inference.
- Data residency: we must ensure U.S. region only.

I’ve attached our procurement form (procurement_form.pdf) and a short internal note on expected month-over-month growth. Once you send formal numbers we can run the PO/Legal review.

—Emma
Director of Platform Engineering | NovaCare
emma.lawrence@novacare.com | +1 (617) 555-2233

Attachments: procurement_form.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lawrence <emma.lawrence@novacare.com>, Hector Ramos <hector.ramos@novacare.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: NovaCare uplift accelerator, co-term & license-swap options

Emma / Hector —

Appreciate the timeline — we can meet the 2027-05-10 PO window if we lock terms this week. Below are modeled examples using your current avg monthly spend ($137k) and the growth cadence you shared. I pulled the attached draft amendment (NovaCare_Renewal_Amendment_v1.pdf) for structure; we can iterate.

Summary numbers (illustrative):

A) Accelerator top-up (6-month uplift, pro-rata)\   - Incremental reserved units: +25% of current average monthly capacity\   - Discount on per-token rate: 10% (applies to uplift portion)\   - Example: effective monthly spend month 1 = $150k, month 3 = $162k (includes uplift + discount)\nB) Annualize + co-term (12-month commit, co-term Nov 2027)\   - Commit = 110% of annualized current run-rate (gives headroom)\   - Blended discount: 15% off PAYG rates across committed units\   - One-time onboarding credit: $20k if signed by 2027-05-03\nC) License-swap to reserved units (swap seat/license $ -> reserved capacity)\   - Convert your seat/licensing spend into reserved units at a blended conversion rate\   - Effective discount range: 18–22% depending on conversion depth\   - Minimum commit: 6 months pro-rata for remainder of year, then annual renewal

SLA & data residency:
- SLA: reserved capacity customers get 99.95% monthly availability SLA (standard addendum) — we'll include the SLA addendum in the amendment.
- Data residency: can restrict to US regions; we will add the region clause to the amendment.

Procurement / Legal notes:
- We can include the onboarding credit ($20k) as an invoice credit line in the amendment.
- For the license-swap we’ll provide a worked example in the cost table showing the conversion and the blended per-token rate.

DocuSign / next steps: I’ll attach a draft amendment and a detailed cost table after Jordan confirms the preferred path. If you confirm Accelerator or License-swap as your preference by EOD Fri (2027-04-23) we’ll push a DocuSign w/ the onboarding credit line and updated SLA.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0199

Attachments: NovaCare_Renewal_Amendment_v1.pdf, Usage_Snapshot_Q1_2027.xlsx

From: Hector Ramos <hector.ramos@novacare.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: NovaCare uplift accelerator, co-term & license-swap options

Kimberly / Jordan —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. A couple of procurement/legal items before we proceed:

- We need the SLA language inserted into the amendment (99.95% with credits schedule). Please include specific remedies (service credits up to 6% of monthly invoice for sustained outages).
- Onboarding credit: procurement would like $30k (not $20k) given the integration work — any flexibility?
- Minimum commit: can we cap the near-term minimum to 6 months for the license-swap (we cannot go annual without exec approval).
- Add a clause for a quarterly usage cap (we want a soft cap and overage protection so spikes don't surprise our finance team).

Small note: we are evaluating a competing offer from ApertureAI — their short-term uplift pricing is slightly lower but they lack the reserved capacity convert option. If you can meet the $30k onboarding and include the quarterly cap language, we can route to Legal for a quick review and aim to sign the DocuSign by 2027-05-03.

Hector Ramos
Procurement Manager | NovaCare
hector.ramos@novacare.com | +1 (617) 555-2240

Attachment: procurement_form.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lawrence <emma.lawrence@novacare.com>, Hector Ramos <hector.ramos@novacare.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: NovaCare uplift accelerator, co-term & license-swap options

Emma / Hector —

Thanks for the quick turn. We can meet you in the middle:
- Onboarding credit: $30,000 (applied as invoice credit on the first month) if signed by 2027-05-03.
- SLA: will include 99.95% with the remedies schedule (service credits up to 6% monthly) in the amendment.
- Quarterly soft cap + overage protection: we’ll add a soft-cap clause and a pre-notice window (30 days) for the first two quarters; overages billed at a capped uplift rate.
- Minimum near-term commit for license-swap: 6 months pro-rata is acceptable; full annualization can be elected at renewal.

Proposed path to close:
1) You confirm Accelerator top-up vs License-swap preference by EOD Tue (2027-04-27).
2) We update the amendment + cost table with the $30k credit, SLA addendum, quarterly cap language and send via DocuSign.
3) NovaCare Legal/Procurement does a quick review; target DocuSign signature by 2027-05-03 so PO can be issued by 2027-05-10.

I’ve asked Marissa to prepare the final cost table and the updated amendment draft; Kimberly will follow up with the DocuSign link once Marissa uploads.

If that timeline works I’ll mark this as priority on our side.

Appreciate the collaboration —
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Next steps: Marissa will send the cost table + DocuSign by EOD Tue.
